yAxis.label: Total power draw required (watts - log scale)

figures.takeaway: The power needed to train a frontier model has risen roughly a millionfold since 2011, from a few hundred watts to over 100 megawatts.

figures.title: Number of public or public-private AI supercomputers, 2010–25
figures.takeaway: State-backed compute is now a geopolitical asset class; China's cumulative count is roughly double North America's.

figures.title: Global private investment in AI, 2013–25

yAxis.label: Total investment (in billions of US dollars)

figures.takeaway: $344.7B of private capital went into AI in 2025 — 127.5% more than 2024, and 67 times the 2013 figure.

figures.title: Global corporate investment in AI by investment activity, 2013–25

yAxis.label: Total investment (in billions of US dollars)

figures.takeaway: $581.69B of corporate AI investment in 2025 - a 129.9% jump on 2024, and about forty times the 2013 total.

figures.title: Global private investment in AI by geographic area, 2013–25

yAxis.label: Total investment (in billions of US dollars)

figures.takeaway: US private AI investment ($285.88B) is roughly 23 times China's, and the gap widened sharply in 2025.

figures.title: Global private investment in generative AI, 2019–25

yAxis.label: Total investment (in billions of US dollars)

series.label: Global private investment in generative AI

figures.takeaway: Generative AI took $170.87B in 2025 - close to half of all private AI investment, and more than triple 2024.

figures.title: Select AI Index technical performance benchmarks vs. human performance

yAxis.label: Performance relative to the human baseline (%)

figures.takeaway: Every benchmark here has been saturated within a few years of release, and the newest ones fall fastest.

figures.title: Share of respondents who say their organization uses AI in at least one function, 2017–25
figures.takeaway: Adoption sat flat around 50–58% for five years, then went near-vertical once generative AI arrived.

figures.title: AI job postings (% of all job postings) by select geographic areas, 2014–25 (part 1)

yAxis.label: AI job postings (% of all job postings)

figures.takeaway: AI demand is concentrating in small, open, services-heavy economies - Singapore leads at 4.69% of all postings.

figures.title: Number of reported AI incidents, 2012–25
figures.takeaway: 362 reported incidents in 2025, up 29% on 2024 and roughly 45 times the 2012 count.

figures.title: Number of AI-related bills passed into law in G20 countries, 2016–25
figures.takeaway: G20 lawmaking peaked at 16 bills in 2024 and fell to 11 in 2025 - the first sustained dip since 2019.

figures.title: Number of AI-related regulations in the United States, 2016–25
figures.takeaway: US federal agency regulation jumped from 25 to 59 in a single year, then flattened at 58.

figures.title: Trust in government regulation of AI by country (% of total), 2025

series.label: Trust in government regulation of AI

figures.takeaway: Only 31% of Americans trust their government to regulate AI properly - the lowest of any country surveyed, against 81% in Singapore.
